record.paper_title: Quo Vadis Strangeness? Strangeness — Open Questions
record.original_question: Why does the specific strangeness yield appear to rise rapidly with increasing collision energy or changing reaction volume between SPS collision systems: because current SPS experiments lie near the threshold to deconfinement, or because the lifespan and dynamics of highly compressed dense quark matter change with collision energy and system size?

evidence.quote: An important aspect here is that the specific yield of strangeness produced seems to fall rapidly with decreasing available collision energy, or increasing reaction volume (or both).
Could it be that this rapid rise in strangeness yield with collision energy occurs since the current SPS experiments occur just at the threshold to deconfinement? Alternatively:

Is it possible that this rapid change in strangeness yield is an intricate effect of the dynamics of highly compressed dense quark matter arising in particular from differences in the lifespan of the high temperature deconfined phase? We need to clarify this important issue.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In ultra-relativistic nucleus–nucleus collisions, define the specific strangeness yield as the number of produced strange quark–antiquark pairs per unit of produced entropy (or, operationally, per produced pion). Empirically, in fixed-target heavy-ion collisions at CERN SPS energies (per-nucleon beam energies in the range of roughly 20–200 GeV), the specific strangeness yield is observed to rise rapidly with increasing center-of-mass collision energy and to vary strongly with the size of the colliding system (reaction volume).

Determine which of the following mechanisms is responsible for this rapid variation:

(a) The explored SPS energy range lies near the threshold of the deconfinement phase transition, so that the rapid change reflects the transition between hadronic matter and a deconfined quark–gluon phase as a function of energy and system size; or

(b) The deconfined phase is already produced throughout the relevant SPS regime, and the rapid variation of the specific strangeness yield is instead controlled by changes in the dynamics and lifetime of the hot, highly compressed deconfined quark matter as the collision energy and system size are varied.

Provide a quantitative, theoretically and experimentally supported identification of the dominant mechanism (or the relative contribution of each), specifying the role of the onset of deconfinement versus the role of fireball lifetime and dynamics in determining the specific strangeness yield at SPS energies.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent NA49 and NA61/SHINE measurements have established anomalous structures ("horn", "kink", "step") in strangeness and pion observables near 30A GeV, widely interpreted as consistent with an onset of deconfinement at SPS energies. However, alternative explanations involving canonical suppression, hadronic dynamics, and fireball lifetime effects remain viable, and the relative weight of "threshold of deconfinement" versus "QGP-lifetime dynamics" mechanisms is still debated as of recent NA61/SHINE results.

status_evidence.title: Investigating the onset of deconfinement with NA61/SHINE
status_evidence.snippet: Several anomalies in energy dependence of hadron production predicted as signals of deconfinement phase transition are observed and they indicate that the onset of deconfinement is located at about 30 A GeV.
status_evidence.claim: Onset of deconfinement is supported by experimental anomalies at SPS, but interpretation remains under active investigation.

status_evidence.title: Results on system size dependence of strangeness production in the CERN SPS energy range from NA61/SHINE
status_evidence.snippet: System size dependence of strangeness production in the CERN SPS energy range from NA61/SHINE
status_evidence.claim: System-size and energy dependence of strangeness at SPS is still being studied experimentally.

status_evidence.title: Strangeness enhancement and energy dependence in heavy ion collisions
status_evidence.snippet: Relative enhancement of strange particle yields from p-p/p-A to A-A collisions substantially increases with decreasing collision energy due in part to canonical suppression.
status_evidence.claim: Alternative (non-deconfinement) explanations of strangeness energy dependence remain in play.
